subtitle: Memory prices a cycle at its peak; contract floors may make this one shallower

thesis.headline: Memory is priced for a peak, but contract floors may make this cycle shallower

bullets.text: MU grew revenue from $37.4 bn in FY'25 to $133.2 bn in FY'26, and 4Q'26 gross margin was 86.8% against 44.7% a year earlier
Take-or-pay customer agreements give MU committed volumes, and customers had deposited $12.7 bn by year end
We adopt the Street's revenue but fade EBITDA margin from 83.0% in FY'27E to 65.0% in FY'31E, so our FY'28E EPS of $163.68 is 20.5% below the Street
At 5.9x NTM EPS, the shares price MU as a cyclical at its peak, and we think the market is too sceptical about how long the revenue lasts

thesis.notes: Open with the call, then the three reasons: growth, contract protection and our more cautious margin.

call.notes: Walk the three cases left to right, then the benchmark line.

business.headline: Micron makes the memory that AI data centers cannot do without

bullets.text: MU makes DRAM, NAND and NOR memory, including high-bandwidth memory built for AI
DRAM generated $28.6 bn (76.5%) of FY'25 revenue and NAND $8.5 bn (22.7%)
Core Data Center revenue reached $18.0 bn in 4Q'26, up from $1.6 bn a year earlier, with gross margin rising from 41.0% to 90.0%
Cloud Memory revenue was $16.3 bn in 4Q'26 alone, and we see it as the unit most exposed to a single group of customers

business.notes: Four business units; the data center units drive the thesis.

mispricing.headline: The Street is right on revenue and, we think, too high on margin

bullets.text: Consensus expects FY'27 revenue of $274.9 bn and FY'28 revenue of $314.2 bn, and our base case takes both as given
Our FY'27E EPS of $159.83 and FY'28E EPS of $163.68 are 9.4% and 20.5% below consensus, because we fade margin
In the year to Sep'22, the last peak, LTM EV/EBITDA had a median of 4.9x, and our 6.0x exit multiple sits inside that range
The 3-year median multiples of 26.4x P/E and 16.1x EV/EBITDA were set on trough and recovery earnings, so they overstate what the market will pay for peak profits

mispricing.notes: The disagreement with the Street is about margin, not sales.

peers.headline: The supply response will come from MU's named competitors

bullets.text: The 10-K names Samsung, SK hynix, Kioxia, Sandisk, CXMT and YMTC as the main competitors in memory and storage
Samsung and SK hynix matter most, because the supply response to today's pricing will come from their capital spending as much as MU's own
Governments have provided and may provide significant assistance to competitors or new entrants, which is the least predictable input to our supply view

peers.notes: We describe the peer group and leave out a trading table.

catalysts.headline: Three dated events decide whether this is a floor or a peak

bullets.text: MU reports 1Q'27 results on 2026-12-23 against guidance of revenue of $61.5 bn plus or minus $1.5 bn
The FY'26 10-K should disclose the share of revenue under contract, the length of the terms and the level of the floor price
The Boise fab projects first DRAM wafers in mid-calendar 2027, and our base case slows revenue growth to 3.0% a year from FY'29E as supply grows

catalysts.notes: Each catalyst is dated and moves the base case by a quantifiable amount.

risks.headline: The cycle, the margin and a narrow rating cushion are the risks that matter

bullets.text: The cycle returns early. Memory revenue fell (49.5%) in FY'23, and gross margin reached (9.1%)
bullets.detail: Revenue could look like our bear case: $180.0 bn in FY'27E and $110.0 bn in FY'28E, a bear target of $306.91 for MU, a (71.1%) return. Mitigant: the agreements are take-or-pay, and net cash of about $68.3 bn can fund a downturn

bullets.text: Margin fades faster than we model. A margin of 55.0% in FY'28E instead of 76.0% would cut that year's EBITDA by about $66.0 bn
bullets.detail: Mitigant: most agreements carry a price floor, and the FY'22 peak EBITDA margin was 54.7%

bullets.text: The rating has a narrow margin of safety. The base case clears the 5.0-point band by only 6.9 points
bullets.detail: A share price above about $1,080 would put the base-case return under the threshold, and the shares are only 1.7% below that level today. We would revisit the rating on any move through those levels

bullets.text: Customers are concentrated, and credit follows them. Receivables reached $36.2 bn at year end, up from $9.3 bn
bullets.detail: If hyperscale buyers delay payment or cancel orders, working capital absorbs cash. Mitigant: MU held $73.5 bn of cash and investments against $5.2 bn of debt

bullets.text: Trade policy and government support for competitors can change the supply picture
bullets.detail: 7.1% of FY'25 revenue came from China and 3.0% from Hong Kong, and the 10-K flags tariffs and export controls as risks

risks.notes: Give the risks as much time as the upside.
